source_text: Well, let's hold off on building this for now, because I have to think about scheduling.  500 hours is 10 weeks of 50 hour weeks.  I'm on sabbatical right now, but I'm focusing on business development not on learning mathematics, so if it's going to be worth my while to do this, I'd need to figure out how to put it into my schedule.  An obvious time to do that would be once I get the War Machine working so that it needs minimal intervention and can code while I do other things.  If I could extend my "3 month sabbatical" to a "6 month sabbatical" with the WM working for me in the 2nd half, then this could work out reasonably well.  Another option would be to rescale to 20 weeks of 25 hour weeks and try to do this "part time" as I do the coding and business development stuff part time.  My sense of the best strategy for now is to NOT be immersive but do a little bit of infrastructure at a time.  So my idea: let's work in M-futonzero-prelim-practice on the *design* of the system rather than building it, and we could take pilots like your 61 closed topology proof survey in stride as we build the actual system.  If I can find 10 or 20 weeks to actually do this at a reasonably immersive pace, I will do it, and if not, I can make it available to others who have more time.
